provenance.reference: Saval A, Minh DP, Chapuis K, Tranouez P, Caron C, Daude E, Taillandier P (2023). Dealing with mixed and non-normative traffic. An agent-based simulation with the GAMA platform. PLOS ONE 18(3): e0281658. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0281658

description: B1 = hand-crafted spec transferred from Saval et al. (2023), the GAMA model of mixed car-motorcycle traffic calibrated on Hanoi video (Tay Son street). Its structure (3 archetypes, the params listed, the rules early_start / swarm_red_running) is the fixed structure in which P1 and B2 tune values (E1). Transferred: Table 11 'Driver parameter values for Hanoi' (IDM a, b, T, s0 -> SUMO Krauss accel, decel, tau, minGap: same meaning, different model, so literature_transferred) and Sec 4 'Description of the model and parameters used' (cars always stop at red, front-row motorcycles stop with probability 0.5; motorcycle lane pitch 0.8 m = 0.7 m width + 0.1 m spacing). Not transferred: the MOBIL parameters of Table 11 (politeness p, threshold athr, bsafe, abias), which have no one-to-one SL2015 counterpart in the bound space (SL2015 defaults kept); vehicle lengths 3.8 / 2 m and max speeds 130 / 60 km/h (geometry and maxSpeed are not in the space; B0 values kept); step 0.5 s (ours 0.1 s); pblock_node and prespect_priorities (no Hanoi values given). The paper has no illegal left turn, no early start and no gap acceptance: those entries are assumed and set to neutral values (rule off or SUMO default) so that only the paper's content changes behaviour vs B0. The illegal_left_box rule is left out (ruling R26): the paper has no box waiting, so the box behaves natively as in B0 (B1 has no M7 lever).

driver_archetypes.rationale: Saval et al. 2023, Table 11 (Driver parameter values for Hanoi, column Car, GA-calibrated on Tay Son): max acceleration a = 1.2 m/s2 -> accel, max deceleration b = 4.8 m/s2 -> decel, time headway T = 2.5 s -> tau, safety distance s0 = 1.1 m -> minGap (IDM -> Krauss, literature_transferred). Sec 4: cars always stop at red, so no red-running rule and the jm* attributes stay at the SUMO defaults (never drive at red). One archetype: the paper has one car driver type.

Saval et al. 2023, Table 11 (column Motorcycle): a = 1.1 m/s2 -> accel, b = 4.6 m/s2 -> decel, T = 0.8 s -> tau, s0 = 1.9 m -> minGap (IDM -> Krauss, literature_transferred). minGapLat: Sec 4 sizes a motorcycle 'lane' as 0.8 m = 0.7 m width + 0.1 m safe spacing, i.e. ~0.1 m lateral gap; 0.1 m is below the lower bound 0.3 m of the space (ruling R15), so the bound 0.3 m is used (transferred and clipped). One archetype: the paper has one motorcycle driver type.

Illegal left-turning motorcycles (vTypeDistribution moto_violator). The car-following and lateral values are the motorcycle values of Saval et al. 2023 Table 11 / Sec 4, as for moto_saval: they are the same riders. jmTimegapMinor = 1.0 s is the SUMO default and is assumed (the paper has no illegal left turn and no gap acceptance); it is in the structure because it is the early-leaving lever of the box waiters (ruling R15) that P1/B2 tune.

traci_rules.rationale: Saval et al. 2023, Sec 4 'Description of the model and parameters used': from the Tay Son footage 'the probability of stopping for motorcycles (in the front row) is only 0.5'; 'a motorcycle arriving at a red light will have only a 50% chance to stop'. Transferred as a constant run-the-red probability p0 = p_max = 0.5 for a motorcycle reaching the stop line during red, k = 0 (the paper has no swarm effect). dt = 10 s is assumed and has no effect while k = 0.

Not in Saval et al. 2023 (assumed): the paper models no early start, so the rule is off (p = 0). It is part of the fixed structure so that P1/B2 can tune the M2 early-start share; t_before_green and v_max are assumed mid-range values without effect while p = 0.
